The text says he did what was right, just as his father Uzziah had done, and then adds, "In addition, he did not enter the temple of the LORD." (2 Chronicles 27:2). Uzziah, Judah's king before him, went in to burn incense and it did not end well (2 Chronicles 26:16-21). So Jotham stays out.

That's right, friend. Jotham stays out of the LORD's temple, and 2 Chronicles 27:2 says so plainly. Uzziah, Judah's king before him, did go in, and leprosy broke out on his forehead (2 Chronicles 26:16-21). So the two kings share one thing, doing what was right in the eyes of the LORD, but they part ways at the temple door.

explanations.answer: He kept his ways right before God
explanations.explanation: Yes, and the text says it outright: "So Jotham grew powerful because he ordered his ways before the LORD his God." (2 Chronicles 27:6). Builder, winner, and the reason given is how he lived before the LORD. Not a trick or a lucky break in sight, friend.

Offerings sound like a good guess, friend, but the text never says that. It says, "So Jotham grew powerful because he ordered his ways before the LORD his God." (2 Chronicles 27:6). The reason is how he ordered his ways. Offerings don't show up in this passage.

explanations.answer: He made peace with the kings around him
